newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish PM not calmed by de Silguy's tax statement.
newsitem.headline: Swedish PM not calmed by de Silguy's tax statement.

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson said on Thursday that he remained wary of possible EU moves to harmonise taxes despite assurances from European Economic Affairs Commissioner Yves Thibault de Silguy.
"I don't know if I am calmer," Prime Minister Goran Persson told reporters. "A few weeks ago, he made a statement to the contrary. We do not know where the discussion will end."
"There is no tax or social precondition attached to EMU," de Silguy told Swedish journalists in Brussels on Thursday ahead of a visit on Friday to Stockholm.
Persson said that the statement was good, although he would like to see harmonised taxes on capital as there were "free-riders," in some countries ayt the moment.
De Silguy also said that no EU member country could be forced to join Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), a position which Sweden's minority Social Democratic government has said all along.
"He has apparently sided with the general opinion," Persson said. "You cannot force a country into a monetary union." -- Barbara Taltavull, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017
